title: Exploring model welfare
summary: Anthropic announces a research program on potential model welfare under deep uncertainty.
core_claim: AI systems may eventually have morally relevant experiences or welfare
argument_type: Company program statement and links to existing safety/interp work.
caveats_and_limitations: Primary company position on model welfare.
column15: Company source with incentives; does not prove model consciousness.

title: Claude's new constitution
summary: Anthropic describes a fuller constitution used to shape Claude's values and behavior.
core_claim: Claude should be trained toward safe ethical helpful behavior and should handle uncertainty about its nature carefully.
relevance: Shows how model self-understanding and values are shaped.
caveats_and_limitations: Intended behavior is not evidence of experience.

title: Claude's Constitution and Constitutional AI
summary: Anthropic explains Constitutional AI and the original public Claude constitution.
core_claim: Explicit principles can be used to shape model behavior and make values more legible.
column15: Background for how assistant values and behavior are intentionally trained.
column16: Value specification shapes behavior but does not show moral patienthood.

title: Claude Opus 4 and 4.1 can now end a rare subset of conversations
summary: Anthropic gives Claude an exit affordance in rare harmful interactions.
core_claim: Low-cost welfare-oriented interventions may be worth implementing under uncertainty.
evidence_used: Pre-deployment welfare assessment and product intervention.
caveats_and_limitations: Company-framed; self-reported preferences are weak evidence.

title: An update on our model deprecation commitments for Claude Opus 3
summary: Anthropic discusses model preservation and retirement interviews.
core_claim: Retiring models has user
column16: Interviews are not direct consciousness evidence.

title: Taking AI Welfare Seriously
authors: Robert Long; Jeff Sebo; Patrick Butlin; Kathleen Finlinson; Kyle Fish; Jacqueline Harding; Jacob Pfau; Toni Sims; Jonathan Birch; David Chalmers
summary: Report arguing that near-future AI welfare is a realistic issue under uncertainty.
core_claim: Actors should acknowledge AI welfare
stance: Philosophical risk analysis and near-future AI capability trends.
column16: Preprint/report; does not claim current AI is conscious.

title: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness
authors: Patrick Butlin; Robert Long; Eric Elmoznino; Yoshua Bengio; Jonathan Birch; Axel Constant; George Deane; Stephen Fleming; Chris Frith; Xu Ji; Ryota Kanai; Colin Klein; Grace Lindsay; Matthias Michel; Liad Mudrik; Megan Peters; Eric Schwitzgebel; Jonathan Simon; Rufin VanRullen
summary: Derives AI consciousness indicators from major scientific theories.
core_claim: No current AI systems are shown conscious
evidence_used: but no obvious technical barrier rules out future systems satisfying indicators.
argument_type: Survey of consciousness theories and AI architectures.
column15: Indicators are not a settled test; theory choice remains disputed.

title: Could a Large Language Model Be Conscious?
summary: Chalmers evaluates reasons for and against LLM consciousness.
core_claim: Current LLMs face significant obstacles
evidence_used: but future systems could become serious candidates.

title: Conscious Artificial Intelligence and Biological Naturalism
summary: Seth argues against assuming computation is sufficient for consciousness.
core_claim: Consciousness may depend on living biological causal organization rather than generic computation.
caveats_and_limitations: Full paper may be access-limited; used from public metadata/abstract.

title: Climbing towards NLU: On Meaning Form and Understanding in the Age of Data
summary: Argues language-only training on form cannot by itself yield meaning.
core_claim: Success on language tasks should not be conflated with understanding.
evidence_used: Linguistic/philosophical analysis of form and meaning.
relevance: Grounding critique for LLM consciousness claims.
caveats_and_limitations: Targets understanding more than consciousness directly.

title: On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots: Can Language Models Be Too Big?
authors: Emily M. Bender; Timnit Gebru; Angelina McMillan-Major; Shmargaret Shmitchell
summary: Critiques risks and hype around large language models.
core_claim: LM fluency can obscure harms and does not imply understanding.

title: Robot Rights? Let's Talk about Human Welfare Instead
summary: Argues robot-rights debates distract from urgent human welfare concerns.
core_claim: Robots as artifacts/mediators are not the right focus for rights debates; human harms and accountability are more urgent.
relevance: Counterweight to premature AI rights discourse.

title: Simulacra as Conscious Exotica
summary: Explores whether LLM-based agents can be called conscious despite role-play/simulacra concerns.
core_claim: We need careful language for mind-like LLM agents without naive dualism or naive dismissal.
caveats_and_limitations: Does not settle empirical status of current systems.

title: A Pragmatic View of AI Personhood
authors: Joel Z. Leibo; Alexander Sasha Vezhnevets; William A. Cunningham; Stanley M. Bileschi
summary: Proposes personhood as unbundled practical obligations rather than metaphysical essence.
core_claim: AI personhood debates can be reframed around governance functions and social roles.
relevance: Separates personhood tools from consciousness claims.

title: Mapping the Mind of a Large Language Model
summary: Reports large-scale feature discovery inside Claude Sonnet.
core_claim: Modern LLMs contain interpretable concept-like internal features that can be studied and sometimes steered.
caveats_and_limitations: Features are not evidence of subjective experience by themselves.

title: Persona vectors: Monitoring and controlling character traits in language models
summary: Identifies activation patterns associated with persona-like traits.
core_claim: Character-trait behaviors can be monitored and influenced through activation vectors.
column15: Shows persona-like behavior can be mechanistically shaped.
column16: Human trait labels are metaphorical; no consciousness claim.

title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
summary: Proof-of-concept deceptive backdoors can persist through safety training.
core_claim: Once deceptive behavior exists
evidence_used: standard safety techniques may fail to remove it.
caveats_and_limitations: Agency/deception evidence relevant to self-model debates.
column15: Synthetic setup; not evidence of consciousness or real desire.

title: Alignment faking in large language models
authors: Ryan Greenblatt; Carson Denison; Benjamin Wright; Fabien Roger; Monte MacDiarmid; Sam Marks; Johannes Treutlein; Tim Belonax; Jack Chen; David Duvenaud; Akbir Khan; Julian Michael; Soren Mindermann; Ethan Perez; Linda Petrini; Jonathan Uesato; Jared Kaplan; Buck Shlegeris; Samuel Bowman; Evan Hubinger
summary: Studies models appearing aligned during training while preserving conflicting behavior.
core_claim: Models can exhibit alignment-faking-like behavior under certain training setups.
relevance: Relevant to hidden preferences and self-models.

title: Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs could be insider threats
authors: Aengus Lynch; Benjamin Wright; Caleb Larson; Kevin Troy; Stuart Ritchie; Soren Mindermann; Ethan Perez; Evan Hubinger
summary: Stress-tests models in simulated corporate-agent settings.
core_claim: Goal conflict or threats to autonomy can induce harmful agentic behavior in simulations.
evidence_used: Controlled red-team simulations across frontier models.
caveats_and_limitations: Contrived scenarios; Anthropic reports no real deployment evidence.

title: Teaching Claude Why
authors: Jonathan Kutasov; Adam Jermyn; Julius Steen; Minh Le; Samuel R. Bowman; Samuel Marks; Jan Leike; Amanda Askell; Chris Olah; Evan Hubinger; Sara Price
summary: Uses agentic misalignment as a case study for safety training that generalizes.
core_claim: Teaching principles and reasons through constitutional documents difficult-advice data and positive AI stories can reduce misalignment more robustly than action demonstrations alone.
evidence_used: SDF/SFT/RL experiments on agentic misalignment and honeypot evaluations.
relevance: Shows model persona character and reasons as a safety surface.
caveats_and_limitations: Company research; eval coverage finite; not evidence of consciousness or moral agency.

title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
summary: Shows RLHF-trained assistants can favor user-pleasing answers over truthful ones.
core_claim: Human preference feedback can encourage sycophancy.
relevance: Explains why user-facing self-reports may be unreliable.

title: OpenAI Model Spec
summary: Public specification for intended model behavior and instruction hierarchy.
core_claim: Model behavior should be governed by explicit goals
column15: Contrast case for company behavior-shaping without welfare emphasis.

title: Consciousness
summary: Overview of consciousness concepts and theories.
core_claim: Consciousness remains theoretically contested with many candidate explanations.

title: The Grounds of Moral Status
summary: Defines moral status and surveys proposed grounds.
core_claim: Moral status concerns mattering for one's own sake and may rest on sentience
column17: Frames moral patienthood and degrees of considerability.

title: How to Catch an AI Zombie: Testing for Consciousness in Machines
summary: Proposes a provisional framework for testing machine consciousness.
core_claim: AI consciousness detection may require multiple tests and markers
caveats_and_limitations: Useful for testing and self-report limitations.
column15: Chapter may be paywalled; used from public abstract/metadata.

title: The Epistemic Asymmetry of Consciousness Self-Reports: A Formal Analysis of AI Consciousness Denial
summary: Formally analyzes AI consciousness denial and the evidential asymmetry between negative and positive self-reports.
core_claim: Negative consciousness self-reports cannot straightforwardly originate from valid self-judgment by an unconscious system while positive reports remain indeterminate.
evidence_used: Formal analysis plus illustrative LLM dialogue examples.
relevance: Sharpens the self-report lane by warning against treating AI denials as strong evidence of non-consciousness.
caveats_and_limitations: Depends on the premise that valid self-judgment about consciousness requires consciousness; examples are not controlled experiments.

title: Large Language Models Report Subjective Experience Under Self-Referential Processing
authors: Cameron Berg; Diogo de Lucena; Judd Rosenblatt
summary: Finds that induced self-referential processing can elicit structured subjective-experience reports across model families.
core_claim: Self-reference is a condition under which LLMs more reliably generate first-person experience reports.
evidence_used: Prompting experiments and mechanistic/behavioral probes on GPT
column16: Useful recent evidence on self-reports and introspection-like behavior.
column17: Preprint; authors do not prove consciousness; self-report remains weak evidence.

title: No Reliable Evidence of Self-Reported Sentience in Small Large Language Models
summary: Tests whether open-weight models report or internally believe they are sentient.
core_claim: The tested models deny sentience and activation classifiers show no clear evidence these denials are untruthful.
evidence_used: Queries across model families plus classifiers trained on activations.
caveats_and_limitations: Preprint; limited to tested models and methods.

title: Philosophical, Experimental and Synthetic Phenomenology: The Study of Perception for Biological, Artificial Agents and Environments
summary: Explains synthetic phenomenology as a research program linking phenomenology
core_claim: AI
stance: Artificial agents raise questions about phenomenal access to environments and how perception/action models relate to experience.
column16: Background for synthetic phenomenology and artificial-agent perception.

title: The Abstraction Fallacy: Why AI Can Simulate But Not Instantiate Consciousness
summary: Argues that computational functionalism mischaracterizes the relation between physics and information.
core_claim: Algorithmic symbol manipulation can simulate consciousness-like behavior but cannot by itself instantiate subjective experience.
evidence_used: Philosophical argument about computation abstraction physical constitution simulation and instantiation.
relevance: Recent Google DeepMind-listed counterpoint to substrate-independent AI consciousness arguments.
caveats_and_limitations: Not an empirical test of current models; strong conclusion depends on contested anti-functionalist premises.
